turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his concern was genuine and that he had reason to believe the Mussulmans were planning to attack the nearby villages.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and asked Nikhil if he was worried about the Mussulmans, or if he just wanted to use the situation to gain some leverage over him.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his dismissive attitude would only embolden the Mussulmans to make their move, and that he should take immediate action to protect his estate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip retorted that Nikhil's warnings were nothing but empty threats, and that he had been dealing with the Mussulmans for years, so he knew how to handle them.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his years of experience did not exempt him from the consequences of his own foolishness, and that the Mussulmans were not to be taken lightly.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil what specific measures he had taken to address the situation, her voice calm and inquiring.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil explained that he had increased the number of guards at the village borders and instructed the villagers to remain vigilant, his voice firm but controlled.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Sandip, her eyes questioning as she wondered aloud if Nikhil's measures might be prudent.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted in derision, asking Nikhil if he thought the Mussulmans would bother a man of his stature, a zamindar with a reputation for being as fierce as he was well-dressed.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that underestimating the Mussulmans' intentions was a grave mistake, and that his own family's safety was at stake.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted in derision, wondering aloud what Nikhil's stake was in predicting doom and gloom, and whether he had suddenly developed a conscience.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and told Nikhil that if the Mussulmans were so eager to attack, perhaps they should just come and take his land, as he was more than happy to give it to them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked, her voice calm and inquiring, what evidence Nikhil had to support his claims of impending attacks.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the intelligence he had received was credible and that the zamindars had a duty to protect their lands and people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip rolled his eyes and told Nikhil that he was starting to sound like a village gossip, always warning him about the Muslims

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his dismissal of the threat was a grave mistake and that he would not be responsible for the consequences of such negligence.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his warnings were as predictable as the monsoons, always raining down the same old doom and gloom on him.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip should not be so cavalier about the situation, as the Mussulmans' discontent was growing by the day.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled, waving his hand in dismissal, and told Nikhil that he was being a melodramatic fool, that the Mussulmans were just a bunch of harmless villagers who wouldn't dare challenge a great zamindar like himself.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's voice turned stern as he told Sandip that such carelessness would be his downfall, and that the zamindar's position was not to be taken lightly.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
